introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information and Communication Technologies (0796), Paper 3 (practical), June 2020. Duration: two hours. Answer ALL tasks.**

The booklet reproduced here contains two versions of the same practical paper, headed DAY 1 and DAY 2: they have the same two tasks (Task A: spreadsheet, 19 marks; Task B: database, 21 marks) with different file names, cell references and wording in a few questions.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is required to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

The working files (the spreadsheet workbook and the database) are supplied on the day in the Candidate folder; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Does the table contain an entire primary key?

Explain your answer. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Yes.** The field **No** (1 to 20) is a complete primary key: it holds a different value in each of the 20 rows, it is never empty, and it identifies one purchase (one line) without help from any other field. (The other fields cannot do this: a name or an item is repeated, and even the pair *Names + Items* is not unique, because *Samson Takang - Spanner* appears in rows 9 and 20 of the table.) The key No is an artificial key made only of a line number: it identifies the line, but it says nothing about the buyer or the item.

*Marking:* 1 mark for "yes, the field No", 1 mark for the explanation (each value is unique and identifies one record).

questions.enonce_markdown:
The General Sales table is not normalised. Give two explanation for this, in the spaces below.

Reason 1.

Reason 2. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two valid reasons (any two):

- **Redundancy (repeated data).** The same buyer name is written again on every purchase (*Gabriel Kome* appears five times) and the same item with the same unit price is written again each time it is sold (*Bulb, 1,500* appears five times). This wastes space and creates update anomalies: changing a price or correcting a spelling means changing many rows, and one missed row leaves the data inconsistent.
- **Non-key fields depend on other non-key fields (transitive dependency).** The Unit Price depends on the Item, not on the key No; the buyer's name describes the buyer, not the line. The table therefore mixes three kinds of data (purchases, buyers, items), which is what the split into the Buyers, Items and Sales tables corrects (third normal form).
- **Calculated field stored.** *Line - Total* = Unit Price x Quantity is derived from two other fields, so it duplicates information and can become wrong when one of them changes (the printed table even contains such a case: see question 8).

*Marking:* 1 mark for each valid reason, correctly explained.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give a reason why the table is in 1NF. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A table is in first normal form (1NF) when every field holds a single, atomic value (no list of values and no repeating group in one cell) and every row can be identified by a key. In the General Sales table each cell contains one value (one name, one item, one number), there are no repeating columns, and the field **No** identifies each row. (It is not in 2NF or 3NF: see question 2.)

*Marking:* 1 mark for the reason (atomic values / no repeating groups / a unique key).

questions.corrige_markdown:
The third table is the table that records each purchase: it must hold the key of a purchase and, as foreign keys, the number of the buyer (from Buyers) and the number of the item (from Items), plus the quantity bought. The unit price is already in Items and the line total is calculated, so neither is stored. The four rows to fill in are:

| Field name | Data type |
|---|---|
| SaleNo (primary key) | AutoNumber (whole number generated by the system) |
| SN (foreign key to Buyers.SN) | Number (Long Integer) |
| ItemNo (foreign key to Items.ItemNo) | Short Text (Text), size 5 |
| Quantity | Number (Long Integer) |

The field names must match the keys of the two other tables (SN and ItemNo), so that the relationships can be created. The primary key of the table is a separate line number (SaleNo, the *No* of the General Sales table) because no combination of buyer and item is unique: *Samson Takang* bought a spanner twice (rows 9 and 20). 

*Marking:* 1 mark for the key fields SN and ItemNo, 1 mark for Quantity (and a key field for the table), 1 mark for suitable data types.

questions.enonce_markdown: Design a simple Entity-Relationship (E-R) diagram of the database in the space below. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each table is an entity; the foreign keys of the third table give the relationships. A buyer can make many purchases but a purchase belongs to one buyer (Buyers 1 - N Sales); an item can be sold many times but a purchase line concerns one item (Items 1 - N Sales):

```
+---------------+ 1        N +---------------+ N        1 +---------------+
| BUYERS        |------------| SALES         |------------| ITEMS         |
| SN (PK)       |   makes    | SaleNo (PK)   | concerns   | ItemNo (PK)   |
| Names         |            | SN (FK)       |            | Item          |
+---------------+            | ItemNo (FK)   |            | UnitPrice     |
                             | Quantity      |            +---------------+
                             +---------------+
```

Buyers and Items are not joined directly: their link is the Sales table (a many-to-many relationship between buyers and items, resolved by an association table).

*Marking:* 1 mark for the three entities with their keys, 1 mark for the two one-to-many relationships correctly placed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Create the *Sales* table in the database and create the relationship according to the E-R Diagram. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a graphical DBMS (MS Access): *Create > Table Design*, enter the four fields of question 4 with their data types, set **SaleNo** as the primary key (key icon) and save the table as **Sales**. Then *Database Tools > Relationships*, add the three tables, drag **Buyers.SN** onto **Sales.SN** and **Items.ItemNo** onto **Sales.ItemNo**, tick *Enforce Referential Integrity* and create. In SQL the same table and relationships are written in one statement (tested with SQLite):

```sql
CREATE TABLE Sales (
    SaleNo   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    SN       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    ItemNo   VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL,
    Quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (SN) REFERENCES Buyers (SN),
    FOREIGN KEY (ItemNo) REFERENCES Items (ItemNo)
);
```

The two `FOREIGN KEY` clauses create the relationships Buyers 1 - N Sales and Items 1 - N Sales: the DBMS then refuses a purchase whose buyer or item does not exist (a test insertion of buyer 42 was refused). 

*Marking:* 1 mark for the table with the right fields and data types, 1 mark for the primary key, 1 mark for the two relationships.

questions.enonce_markdown: Populate the Sales table by obtaining data from the General Sales table. *[3 marks]*

Create a query that reproduces the General Sales table (with fields, SN, Names, Items, Unit Price, Quantity, Line Total). Take note that *Line Total* is a calculated field.

Save the query as **General Sales**. *[3 marks]*

Write, in the line below, the formula in the calculated field found in the query.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The query joins the three tables (Sales with Buyers on SN, Sales with Items on ItemNo) and shows the fields requested; **Line Total** is a calculated field that multiplies the unit price (held in Items) by the quantity (held in Sales). In the query design grid of MS Access the calculated field is typed in a column of the *Field* row:

```
Line Total: [Unit Price]*[Quantity]
```

(written `[Items].[UnitPrice]*[Sales].[Quantity]` if the field names are qualified). The same query in SQL (tested with SQLite):

```sql
SELECT Buyers.SN, Buyers.Names, Items.Item AS Items, Items.UnitPrice AS [Unit Price],
       Sales.Quantity, Items.UnitPrice * Sales.Quantity AS [Line Total]
FROM (Sales INNER JOIN Buyers ON Sales.SN = Buyers.SN)
     INNER JOIN Items ON Sales.ItemNo = Items.ItemNo
ORDER BY Sales.SaleNo;
```
